It also reported that poverty fell from 41.9 percent in 2018 to 36.3 percent in 2022, while extreme poverty was unchanged and lack of health-care access more than doubled.","notes":["The excerpt supports these administration-wide findings and 2018–2022 welfare figures, but does not establish that they were reported specifically as events of 2023."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0003-E010","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"HRW reported that authorities resolved just over 1 percent of crimes committed in 2022; torture was widely practiced, arbitrary detention remained widespread, and mandatory pretrial detention and arraigo violated human-rights standards. A July appellate ruling allowed some challenges to mandatory detention, while military and navy detentions were often not recorded in the National Detention Registry.","notes":["The excerpt attributes the just-over-1-percent figure to crimes committed in 2022, not crimes committed in 2023."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0003-E011","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"As of August 2023, more than 266,000 soldiers, marines, and National Guard members were deployed domestically. Government data recorded 5,488 civilians killed by the army from 2007 through July 2023, and the killings were rarely independently investigated. The military obstructed Ayotzinapa and Cold War-abuse investigations, while the government reportedly asked the missing-person registry managers to manipulate the data to reduce the number reported missing after the total surpassed 110,000.","notes":["The excerpt supports a reported government request to manipulate and reduce the registry, but not the broader wording that the government was merely accused of attempting to relabel it."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0003-E012","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0003-E013","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0003-E014","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0003-E015","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0003-E016","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0003-E017","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0003-E018","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0003-E019","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"Anti-corruption enforcement under López Obrador was described as politicized and generally ineffective: opponents were publicly targeted, while investigations involving allies and favored institutions were rare or perfunctory. Transparency was weakened by military opacity, infrastructure exemptions, López Obrador’s repeated attacks on the press, and attacks against media workers that increased substantially.","notes":["The excerpt supports military opacity, infrastructure exemptions, press attacks, and increased attacks against media workers, but does not include blocked appointments to the transparency agency."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0003-E020","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"Mexico guaranteed formal assembly and NGO freedoms, but police used excessive force and arbitrary detention against protests; Pegasus surveillance concerns persisted; the government’s protection mechanism was sluggish and subject to government neglect. The judiciary suffered delays, corruption, weak prosecutorial autonomy, preventive detention, and limited accountability for military abuses. Ayotzinapa investigations were reported as obstructed, while the National Guard represented continued militarization.","notes":["The excerpt describes the protection mechanism as sluggish and subject to government neglect, but does not state that it was underfunded."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0003-E021","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"Freedom House reported that López Obrador’s administration increased some forms of redistributive spending and the minimum wage, but migrant enforcement under National Guard orders generated serious rights abuses; women’s services faced funding cuts and the president dismissed feminists as political opponents. Legal protections for LGBT+ people and workers expanded, while inequality and exploitation persisted.","notes":["The excerpt does not support the claim that disability-rights protections expanded."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0003-E022","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]}]}
